There’s a lot going on. Let’s start at the very beginning of this. You have a new job since last time you were on the show. Last time, you were the head of Direct-to-Consumer — you were basically the head of Peacock and the other apps inside the family. Now you’re the chairman of NBCUniversal Media Group.
What’s the new job? What does that mean?

NBCUniversal Media Group is comprised of certain services within NBC. It’s the broadcast network, it’s Bravo, it’s Peacock, it’s NBC Sports. We also have NBC News and Telemundo. One of the things that we recognized, especially when we spun off some of our cable assets last year into Versant, was that the assets we had truly worked better together. NBC has been like a megaphone. Given the reach of NBC, it’s been incredibly strategic in growing Peacock, which is a bit ironic because I think so many people believed that broadcasting was a bit of a relic of the past in this digital world, but it’s actually proven to be the opposite. As things have gotten more fragmented, having a broadcast network is actually a superpower because we’re continuing to see ratings growth. That has been really helpful as we’ve been building out Peacock.

But actually, Peacock was also finding new audiences, like cord cutters or people who maybe didn’t grow up watching NBC or some of our cable networks. So, Peacock’s also been really strategic in reaching and driving people back to NBC and Bravo. So, I think that flywheel is where we recognized that we needed to start operating differently. I’ve been a huge advocate of what I like to call “centers of excellence” in how I like to structure the business, which is, content first and platform second. How do we get maximum reach, maximum engagement? That really required us thinking differently about how we were running the business.

Essentially, instead of having a programming group within broadcast and a programming group within streaming, we just collapsed the business. Now you’ve got one programming team, one marketing team, one product and technology team, one decision sciences and research team, and one advertising team. They’re all incentivized around continuing to grow the portfolio, get that maximum reach, maximum engagement, and drive top-line revenue. I think that structure, which we put in place about 18 months ago, is contributing to a lot of the success that we’re seeing now.

Even if you look at 2026, NBC is the number one network in total viewers. We had an unbelievable early part of the year with “Legendary February,” which you might remember. That’s when we had the Super Bowl, the Milan Cortina Olympics, and the NBA All-Star Game. In 17 days, we reached over 225 million viewers. This summer, we had Love Island, which was the number one show of the summer for streaming. You had the World Cup, which was the number one Spanish-language sporting event in US history on Telemundo and Peacock. We had a show called The Five-Star Weekend, which was our number one scripted drama.

Now, we’ve led ourselves into the fall, where we have Sunday Night Football, which has been the number one show for 15 consecutive years. We had a great kickoff with over 25 million viewers. We just had the NBA tip-off last week with the Knicks and the Sixers, which is the number one rated tip-off in NBA history. So, it does feel like we’re firing on all cylinders in how we’re trying to operate with this, again, content-first-platform-second mantra.

But just to go one level deeper, a big part of this strategy is figuring out how do we move audiences across platforms. For example, when I mentioned that Love Island was the number one streaming show of the summer, 40 percent of those Love Island viewers also tuned in to watch the World Cup. So, migrating viewers back and forth across the portfolio is a critical part of how we see ourselves continuing to grow. But to effectuate that, you need to structure yourself in a way where people are incentivized along that vision. We’re still evolving as an organization, but I’m really proud of some of the milestones and accomplishments that we’ve made as a team. I love my job. I feel like I’ve got the best job in the industry at the moment.

It is a tumultuous time in Hollywood, and you seem like one of the happiest people in the industry right at the second. That is very notable. You’re a Decoder pro, you brought up structure. I’m dying to ask you about the Decision Sciences Group. That’s the other question I ask everybody.

But let me just back out for one second. You’re describing quite a lot of freedom in rethinking how something like NBCUniversal would work. You mentioned the Versant spin, so CNBC, MS Now, and a bunch of channels went that way. I’m on its networks all the time. I would describe the folks at Versant as feeling more free. They’re disconnected from the battleship that was Comcast and NBCUniversal. They can go try whatever they want to try. They’re energized by it in some ways.

Then, Comcast looked at NBCUniversal and said, “We’re going to spin off that off as well. We’re going to be the cable business and NBCUniversal will be the entertainment business, and now you’re in charge of that.” You’re like a 20-year Comcast veteran. I think you got your start doing cable boxes.
Yep. I started in 2004 at Comcast.

Just tell me about that process. We spun off CNBC and MS Now into Versant. Now we’re looking at this company. We ought to spin off NBCUniversal as well. Just tell me about how that came about. What was that moment like? Did you all sit in a boardroom? Did it come down from on high? How did that happen?

Well, that decision really was made by Brian Roberts and Mike Cavanagh. Candidly, I was not in the room when that decision was made, but I think if you were to ask people at NBCUniversal, it makes strategic sense.
Do you feel that same sense of freedom?

You know what? I think that there’s an energy. When people show up here, they feel very passionate about what they do. They believe in our strategy, they believe in our portfolio. Look at NBCUniversal more broadly. Before, I was describing the Media Group, but that is one piece of the broader company. You have Universal Pictures and Universal Television, which have obviously been having an unbelievable summer with The Odyssey and Obsession. You’ve got Universal’s theme parks and experiences. We opened up Epic Universe last year. We opened up a kids theme park in Texas. We announced we’re going to open up a theme park in the UK. We have Sky, which was part of the company but more squarely sat within Comcast Cable. Now that’s going to migrate over to the new NBCUniversal as part of this restructure. Then, you have these media assets, which I spoke about earlier.

So, you’ve got this unbelievable portfolio. I think that people here really believe in our growth and that if we’re a separate company, it’s going to allow us to move faster. It’s going to let us have more clarity around where we want to make capital allocations and decisions. There are a few areas that really play to our strengths as an organization. One of them is live sports and live events. That’s always been a part of NBCUniversal that we’re really known for. If you just look at the sports portfolio that we have, Nilay, we’ve got NFL, NBA, MLB, the Big Ten Conference, the Premier League. We’ve got the Olympics with the IOC. You’ve got this unbelievable portfolio of sports content, and that’s a strategic asset when we’re partnering with the leagues because we believe in broadcast. We believe in broad reach. We’re not trying to put everything exclusively on a streaming platform. In 2026, we’ve demonstrated across almost every single sport that we can actually continue to grow ratings and reach new audiences, which is something that’s becoming more and more complicated.

Can I ask about that? Because you also run Peacock, which is a paid streamer where you can access sports. When you say grow ratings on broadcast, are more people putting up antennas to watch sports over the air?
No. What I mean… By the way, about 20 percent of TV households in this country do still use over-the-air antennas as—
Oh, we have lots of listeners who are going to tell you that’s the best picture quality you can get.
Yeah. It is amazing picture quality, especially if you live in the right look angle where you could pick up the signal.

It comes back to what I said earlier about managing as a portfolio. We don’t think of it as a broadcast business sitting next to a streaming business. We really position ourselves as a digital-first company trying to get that maximum reach. When we look at the ratings, we’re combining what you would think of as more traditional ratings for linear television with streaming and all of our digital platforms. Whether that’s DVR or TV Everywhere, we aggregate it into one platform. When you look at it through that lens, which is just audience, we’ve actually demonstrated that across almost every sport — NFL, NBA, or MLB — the total viewers that we are reaching now are, in some cases, the highest they’ve been in decades.

Even the Super Bowl, which we had earlier this year on NBC, reached about 137 million viewers at its peak, and that’s across all of our platforms. That Super Bowl was the highest-rated live event in NBC’s 100-year anniversary, which is this year. It’s kind of counterintuitive, but what we’re showing is that when we start operating as one, we can reach new audiences and we can aggregate them. We are demonstrating that not just across sports. There’s even something like the Thanksgiving Day Parade, which has been an institution on NBC for 99 years. This past Thanksgiving Day Parade was the highest-rated parade we have had in the company’s history. So, there’s a renaissance happening around live. In a world of instant gratification, on demand, and watching what you want when you want, the fact that you’re now seeing more and more viewers wanting the collective consciousness of social viewing, things that still matter in today’s society, that actually plays to our strengths. And we’re seeing that manifest itself with higher ratings.

But as I mentioned, it’s also a big part of our strategy. It was a big part of our Peacock strategy, which was a bit of an anomaly when we launched Peacock six years ago. It’s also a huge part of what I think NBC does well, which is that we create these big tentpole events and we’re able to shine a light on them and get huge audiences that are continuing to show up, even in a world of fragmentation and cord-cutting.

It’s interesting that you’ve described it as content first and platform second, and then you’re describing your approach to ratings as agnostic to distribution. You’re just sort of combining everything and saying, “This is the number of people we reached.”

Well, take something like the Milan Cortina Olympics. This is an interesting example. If you were to look at that Winter Olympics, we had roughly 3,200 hours of content. There’s no way we can make all of that available on one network. There’s no way to daypart 3,200 hours. If you remember what we did with the Paris Olympics, we made the decision to make every event available live. When you make it all available live, we put it all on Peacock. This was a very controversial decision because the question has always historically been that if people tune in to watch this live during the day on Peacock, are they going to tune in to watch NBC primetime? Are we going to cannibalize our ratings or are we going to grow the ratings? This is where we really tested this strategy. If we’re truly indifferent, then what should happen is that we should be able to expand the funnel during the day, get more people into the Olympics, and try to create an experience that we’re very proud of.

We really do believe, whether it was the Gold Zone or Multiview, that we were able to surprise and delight viewers and make it really easy to navigate and find all of the choices on Peacock. But then what happened was that people were tuning in to watch NBC during primetime because there’s a difference between what NBC does and what Peacock does. NBC was more about storytelling. It was more about, “Let’s talk about what happened today. What about the backstory of the athletes? How’s Mike Tirico going to address his perspective on things?” When you combine these two things together — putting all the content on Peacock and then having the primetime show — this Winter Olympics had about a 96 percent higher rating. About 25 million viewers were tuning in to watch the Milan Cortina Olympics, which was about 96 or 97 percent higher than Beijing. On the digital side, it was double the digital minutes of every other Winter Olympics combined. We also doubled the advertising revenue.

You’ve got to be willing to break some glass. This is going to seem so obvious, but it starts with the consumer. It starts with, “How do we approach the consumer and give them the best experience?” And if you build it, they will come. The only reason I’m using the Olympics as an example is because if you were to look at the past, this was a real pain point where we didn’t make everything available on streaming or it was confusing for some viewers to figure out how to navigate all of the choices. We really, as an organization, decided to put our shoulder behind this, and I think the results ultimately speak for themselves. But again, it ladders back up to this vision of really starting to manage as one portfolio. If you can drive that maximum reach and engagement, that’s also going to be where you’ll get the best monetization.
The Verge team in particular was addicted to Gold Zone, which was the whip-around coverage of every medal event. It was very fun.

Let me ask you about this. A big Decoder trope is that your distribution fundamentally affects what you make, right? That the medium is essentially the message, and I know what a YouTuber makes because they’re on YouTube, and I know what a TikToker makes because they’re on TikTok. I could stretch this all the way back and say I know what broadcast TV looks like because the medium of broadcast TV has fundamentally shaped the content that gets made there. I know what cable shows on Bravo look like, and they’re not the same thing and they haven’t been for a while.

You’re describing, “We’re going to bring programming in, we’re going to centralize that, we’re going to be agnostic to distribution — or indifferent I think is the word you used — and that’s going to increase viewership.” But the pressure of the different distributions is still there, right? Running the broadcast network over the air is still different and reaches different people than distributing on YouTube TV, than running Peacock as a paid platform unto itself. How do you manage that tension? Because it is real.

Yeah, it is very real. It’s a really insightful question. The tension is real, but actually, I don’t view it as tension. I view it as an opportunity because you’ve got different audiences. If it’s a Venn diagram and you look at who’s the audience on broadcast versus the audience on cable versus the audience on streaming, there’s some overlap, but it’s not as much as you would think. That actually speaks to this broader strategy, which is, “How do we reach?” If we reach all these different viewers but they’re on different platforms, how do we start bringing this together into one?

Now there’s multiple ways to effectuate that kind of a strategy. One is you start sharing content and window content differently across platforms. For example, we have a show on Peacock called The Paper. Greg Daniels created it, who also created The Office. It’s a really great comedy and it’s an original. If you were to look at how streaming services typically make originals available, they’re exclusive. You premiere it on your streaming platform, and it typically stays on that platform forever.

What we’re starting to experiment with is, well, what if we premiere The Paper on Peacock but then introduce it onto NBC six months later? Now you’re bringing a show that was created for streaming and making it available on NBC to a new audience. You also have this added message, which is that if you want to watch next week’s episode now, go get Peacock. All of a sudden, NBC is not only reaching new audiences but it’s also becoming a sales channel for driving people back to sign up for Peacock.

Do you give that to Greg Daniels? The feedback loop of a YouTuber is so blunt. I’ve made a handful of Instagram Reels in my life. I literally open and look at the retention chart and think, “Oh, I should put another hook in there in the middle to keep my viewers,” and it’s immediate. That’s not even how my brain works. It’s immediate that the data makes you think this way. If you say to Greg Daniels, “Hey, make sure episode two of The Office ends on a cliffhanger so that I can advertise watching the next episode right away on Peacock.

Well, Donna Langley, who oversees all of the entertainment programming, would be the one calling Greg Daniels and giving him that feedback. But here would be a different way to answer that question. I don’t think we’re necessarily trying to change the framework of how some of the shows are being created on NBC or Peacock. There’s still something about premium content and how that’s being created that I think resonates with a lot of people.
c8eb22cbb89f3d32: Victim organizations are losing millions of dollars in token charges as criminals hijack their corporate LLM access to steal expensive computing resources and AI services.

These fraudulent charges from resource consumption can exceed $100,000 a day, according to a Monday report by Google's Mandiant incident responders, who saw cumulative charges at some organizations hit $1 million before the victim companies revoked intruders' access.

"Whenever possible, threat actors want to use this technology to gain a scale advantage over defenders. They achieve that with agentic tools and by stealing tokens from unwitting third parties,” John Hultquist, chief analyst at Google Threat Intelligence Group, told The Register. “Locking down these resources will not only protect organizations from runaway costs, but also protect the broader community from a deluge of cheap, autonomous attacks.”

This tactic of hijacking access to LLMs is called LLMJacking, and it’s been increasing steadily over the past two years. In one extreme case, documented in an August report from CrowdStrike, a token thief sent about 200,000 API requests in just two minutes.

In one case detailed in the report, a group Google tracks as UNC6993 illicitly gained access to LLM API keys, then generated additional keys and enabled services within the victim’s cloud projects, racking up $100,000 in charges.

The threat intel biz also documented a different token thief subscribing victim accounts to Pay-As-You-Go agreements to access advanced models on the victim company’s dime. The crook selected premium foundation models, launched high-volume inference streams, and used a “burn and rotate strategy” to bypass rate limits by creating and deleting short-lived service accounts while auditing the billing interface to monitor financial impact.

In yet another incident, an intruder executed more than 500,000 LLM API calls in less than eight hours using stolen third-party API keys to power a token routing service called Jet Night, according to a Monday report from Google.

“Given Jet Night’s per-token costs to users are so far below typical market rates GTIG believes the service relies on stolen keys to operate profitably,” the report says. “For example, Jet Night offers an unlimited token plan for approximately $60 USD per month with alleged access to frontier models, a consumer service level that would typically run between $100 and $250 per month.”

Jet Night has also admitted to multiple outages on its public Telegram channel, which the Google threat hunters note is “likely due to stolen keys being revoked as victims discover their respective compromises.”

As more criminals join the LLMJacking ecosystem, Google says it has documented a division of labor between the criminals that establish initial access to compromised cloud and AI services, and those that manage downstream monetization infrastructure, called “LLM Mixers.”
In one case that Mandiant responded to in mid-2026, UNC6993 compromised a cloud instance through a misconfigured Service Account key and used this access to grant further access to a model API.

The crooks also spun up a session hijacking page purporting to be an application portal to join a group of LLM users. “This page tricks users into navigating to the legitimate LLM service website, and pasting their raw JSON payload containing an active access token, which was then posted to the backend API to bypass password and multifactor authentication (MFA) controls,” the report says.

Google predicts miscreants will “increasingly prioritize LLMJacking” compared to other types of resource theft like cryptojacking. And to prevent cloud LLM service abuse, the security firm says defenders should prioritize identity and access management plus supply chain security, and use a centralized secrets management platform to rotate keys and secrets.

Also apply least-access privileges to users and service accounts, ensuring that they only have permissions necessary to complete their roles and tasks. And automate secrets scanning within codebases to identify and then remove any API keys and secrets added to source code. ®
929f93aa479841f9: MELAKA: Melaka police have received six election-related reports since yesterday, including four involving damage to or the loss of political parties' campaign materials.
Police chief Datuk Dzulkhairi Mukhtar said the complaints involved campaign flags being broken, removed, torn, burnt and damaged in several state constituencies.
He said the reports received yesterday included the loss of or damage to 22 campaign flags in Ayer Keroh, while about 150 Pakatan Harapan (PH) flags in Rumbia were believed to have been broken.
Police also received reports of PH flags allegedly being removed in Ayer Limau and Parti Bersama campaign materials being damaged in Paya Rumput, he said in a statement.

Dzulkhairi said police had also received a report concerning remarks by Seremban MP Anthony Loke Siew Fook on the disclosure of the pardon minutes involving former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
The case is being investigated under Section 4(1) of the Sedition Act 1948 and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
Another report was lodged in Jasin over the alleged distribution of food baskets and cash estimated at RM50 in conjunction with Deepavali.
The incident was also linked to the presence of a Barisan Nasional (BN) candidate's representative. The case is being investigated under Section 10 of the Election Offences Act 1954, he said.
Dzulkhairi said the Criminal Investigation Department was investigating the reports to identify those involved.
Earlier, Parti Bersama candidate for Paya Rumput Abdul Rashid Abu Bakar alleged that his party's campaign materials had been damaged, including being set on fire.
He said party election workers discovered the damage between 4am and 7am yesterday. An inspection near the Jalan Bukit Rambai bridge found several flagpoles broken and one flag burnt.
d5d6ba4423852e46: SINGAPORE: Binance's customers have withdrawn a net $4.72 billion from the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange since it reopened, after hackers stole around US$6.3 billion of crypto from the platform in what could be the largest financial heist in history.
The exchange froze withdrawals for about 48 hours after the hack, which which the FBI said was carried out by North Korea, then started allowing customers to withdraw again on Sunday morning.
The theft has underlined the vulnerability of digital assets to attacks and raised questions about the impact on Binance, which has vowed to repay customers in full, and on the wider market.
Binance said the net outflows amounted to around 3% of assets on the platform, a relatively modest figure that analysts said suggested customer confidence had largely held up.
"The majority of the withdrawals from the platform were in the form of Tether's USDT stablecoin," Binance added.
The outflow compares with about US$7 billion withdrawn from Circle's USDC stablecoin over a week after the collapse of Silicon Valley Bank in 2023.
Binance itself processed net outflows of about US$6 billion over 72 hours in 2022 after the collapse of FTX.
The attack marks a step-up in North Korea's crypto thefts. Blockchain analytics firm TRM Labs said North Korea-linked hackers have stolen US$7.4 billion so far in 2026.

Analysts and crypto experts said the fallout appeared limited so far, and there was little sign of an impact on broader financial markets despite a deepening of ties between crypto and mainstream finance in recent years.
"Binance will absorb the financial impact of the stolen funds, not our users," the company said in a statement on X.
Binance said it was covering the losses with company funds and had already raised US$6 billion from its corporate treasury, an insurance fund and reserves set aside for security breaches.
"It has not yet triggered widespread panic or a massive, concentrated withdrawal," said Tim Sun, a senior researcher at HashKey Group, a digital asset financial service company in Hong Kong.

Binance, which says it has more than 335 million users worldwide and average daily trading volumes of US$95 billion across digital assets and derivatives, said it had also seen US$2.7 billion in customer inflows since Sunday and that withdrawal volumes were stabilising after an "initial spike".
No rush to withdraw
Some traders told Reuters they were keeping their accounts.
Ryan Tan, a Binance user, said he was in no hurry to withdraw his funds from the platform, as he had already kept his account fairly light since the collapse of FTX four years ago.
"After the FTX collapse, I decided to hold everything on my wallet instead of leaving them on exchanges," said the 39-year-old.
After hitting a six-week low on Friday, Bitcoin prices recovered through the weekend to trade near $78,000 on Monday, while Ether (ETH) also rebounded from a two-month low.

Stablecoin market capitalisations, often viewed as a gauge of money moving into and out of crypto markets, have fallen since Friday, suggesting some investors have shifted funds into cash or traditional assets.
Binance started allowing US dollar cash withdrawals again on Monday.
"Highly complex" money laundering
The FBI said on Saturday that the North Korean state-sponsored group TraderTraitor was responsible for the attack.
Researchers describe the group as highly sophisticated and say its activities help fund the country's weapons programmes.
Analysts said the attack's scale could curb institutional appetite for cryptocurrencies.

Spot bitcoin ETFs recorded outflows of US$643 million on Friday, the largest daily withdrawal in October, while more than US$1.3 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated, according to Ari Redbord, global head of policy at TRM Labs.
"A hack at a crypto exchange is bank robbery at the speed of the internet, which creates an unstable risk profile for anyone responsible for other people's capital," he said.
About half of the stolen funds were held in stablecoins and have been frozen by issuers including Circle, which said on Monday it had frozen more than US$1.1 billion in USDC.

Blockchain research firm Elliptic said around US$3.24 billion of stolen crypto is being held by wallet addresses linked to the theft, describing the laundering process as "highly complex and clearly automated".

Jonathan Benton, founder and chief executive at crypto asset recovery firm iSanctuary, said the technology exists to trace stolen funds, but the challenge is turning that intelligence into rapid, coordinated action before those assets disappear.

"The future of crypto won't be decided by how much money enters the market, but by how safe that money is once it's there," said Benton, former head of the international corruption unit of the UK's National Crime Agency.
ff816c157412d0a9: SUBANG: A man had to carry his elderly parents to safety after flash floods hit Kampung Melayu Subang oday, with floodwaters rising rapidly to waist level.
Zulkarnain Hashim, 46, said he carried his 90-year-old mother and 89-year-old father to higher ground as the water surged.
He said there was a heavy downpour from 2 pm to 4 pm, before water levels rose abruptly to waist level by 5pm.
"It was complete chaos when the water rose so quickly. I had to carry both my mother and father to get them to safety.
"This is not the first time. The flood problem has persisted since 1995, and this year alone our area has been flooded three times," he told Bernama.
Zulkarnain also claimed the neighbourhood's flood warning siren did not sound during the incident, raising questions about the effectiveness of the early warning system
Meanwhile, a 24-year-old mother faced an anxious ordeal getting her two children, including her four-month-old baby, out of their home as floodwaters began rising.
Nur Atilia Elina Rosli said her husband, Ahmad Nawi Yaman, 27, was at work when the water started rising around 3.20pm, just as their baby woke from a nap.
She acted swiftly to move the baby and their three-year-old child out of the house.
"It was chaotic because I have a baby. When we left, the water was already knee-deep. I had to wade through the water carrying my children to reach a house on higher ground.
"This is the worst flood we have experienced so far. The water reached chest level," she said when met at the temporary relief centre at Dewan Siantan, Kampung Melayu Subang.
Earlier, three victims, including a disabled elderly man and an infant, were evacuated to the relief centre following the afternoon deluge.

Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call at 5.18pm, and a fire engine from the Bukit Jelutong Fire and Rescue Station arrived at the scene at 5.33 pm.
He said the flash flood affected about 92 houses across four roads, namely Lorong Merbau (30 houses), Jalan Cengal (seven), Jalan Resak (five), and Jalan Jati (50).

ebe75ecab6e422f9: SEATED outside a church, Saradhadevi Thadcanamoorty recites four handwritten pages of names — 124 husbands, fathers and brothers who vanished during Sri Lanka's civil war.
The Tamil woman, in her 60s, then picked up a placard and with three others started a "march for justice" in the busy eastern city of Batticaloa — their 1,604th consecutive day of protest.
From 1983 to 2009, Sri Lanka was ravaged by war between government forces representing the Sinhalese majority and Tamil separatist rebels, members of a largely Hindu minority.
Over 100,000 people were killed, including many civilians, according to United Nations estimates.
Tens of thousands also disappeared, or were abducted, tortured or killed by security forces or the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE).
More than 15 years after the war ended, the fate of most remains unknown.
Complaints, court appeals, protests, international pressure and repeated government promises have brought little progress.
Thadcanamoorty's story reflects the horrors of the war and the families' long search for answers.
In July 1992, her husband Nallathambi, 34, was found dead in his field, shot in the head.
Witnesses said a soldier had killed him. His wife immediately reported the soldier to the police.
"They told me, 'If you say your husband was killed by a soldier, they will never give him back to you'," she said.
"So I ended up filing a complaint against an unknown person. I recovered his body, received compensation of 50,000 rupees (US$151 at current rates), and the investigation stopped."
In January 2000, her son Navaneethan, 19, disappeared. She believes Tamil rebels abducted him to force him into their ranks.

"I never saw him again," she said. "In 2016, I filed a request for information with the authorities. They replied that his fate was unknown. All I was given was a certificate of disappearance — not the truth."
Lakshmi Silva has found little more certainty.
In July 1990, her husband disappeared while travelling by bus to Colombo. Armed men took him away at a checkpoint.
"Witnesses told me they were 'Tigers'," she said, referring to the rebels.
Her appeals to police and the separatists went unanswered. Those she approached warned her not to make trouble.
In 1994, a magistrate issued a death certificate. The cause of death was listed as "unknown". Since then, nothing.
"I no longer think he will come back," Lakshmi Silva admitted. Now in her 60s, she has tried to move on. "I live only for my children now," she said.
Others refuse to accept the silence.
"I have always kept hoping," said Rajeshwari Chithiravadivel, 61.
On her wall hangs a charcoal portrait of a smiling, moustachioed man, pictured between his wife and daughter.
Her husband disappeared in February 1989, abducted by masked men while shopping. The authorities issued her a death certificate in 1998.
Two years later, the Red Cross presented her with the body of a man for identification, saying it might be her husband.
"He was unrecognisable," she said. "So I continue to believe."

It is for cases like this that the women continue their daily protest, echoing Argentina's Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo, who marched for years demanding answers about the children who disappeared under the country's 1976-1983 dictatorship.
"We secretly hoped thousands of people would join us, but clearly that is not the case," said Sarala Emmanuel, one of the most regular marchers and a campaigner.
"But nothing has changed — there is still a great silence," she said.

Since 2009, Sri Lankan civil society, international rights groups and the United Nations have repeatedly urged successive governments to investigate wartime crimes and bring those responsible to justice.
The election of Anura Kumara Dissanayake as president in 2024 rekindled hopes.
In his election manifesto, the country's first left-wing president promised to probe "political assassinations, disappearances and assaults" and open an independent national prosecutor's office.
Two years on, some progress had been made, said Human Rights Watch in September, but the government had failed to address "the urgent need to end impunity".

"Successive governments are worried to take any steps," said Rasamanikham R. Shanakiyan, a Tamil opposition lawmaker, noting most are Sinhala Buddhists, and that top security officials were reluctant.
"They know that it'll come back to them."

61a5560af2dc3d17: MADRID: Spain has returned to Morocco more than a dozen sub-Saharan African and Asian migrants who reached the Spanish enclave of Ceuta and were turned down for asylum, the first deportation of its kind from the enclave since a mass border crossing in July.
The interior ministry said the group had been sent back to Morocco after it agreed to receive them and they remained on Moroccan territory at present.
It declined to give numbers or nationalities, but migrant and rights charities operating in Ceuta said 16 people from Senegal, Nigeria, Yemen, Cameroon and Bangladesh were deported.

The NGOs claim such returns fail to take into account the risks associated with Morocco's treatment of migrants from other countries and fly in the face of the values espoused by Spain's leftist government.
Virginia Alvarez, an Amnesty International researcher, said Spain's posture was hypocritical.

"Spain, despite its (progressive) speeches in Europe, is not ensuring that human rights guarantees are met for people who cross its borders in Ceuta and Melilla," she said. "Morocco does not respect many human rights," she added.
Morocco's interior ministry did not respond to Reuters requests for comment.

The International Organization for Migration (IOM), which cooperates with Moroccan authorities on voluntary return programmes for third country nationals or migrants, told Reuters IOM does not participate in deportations or forced removals.

"Decisions on removals are the sovereign responsibility of States, and IOM has no role in determining who is removed or where they are sent," it said, adding that its voluntary return programme supports migrants to rebuild their lives after choosing to go back to their countries of origin.

A spokesman for Spain's interior ministry told Reuters that Morocco is considered by the EU to be a safe country, and deportations are carried out "with all the necessary safeguards", without providing further details.
Over 48 hours in July, some 80,000 people crossed from Morocco into Ceuta, a tiny enclave that, along with Melilla, represents Europe's only land borders with Africa.

While most returned within days, thousands remain and prime minister Pedro Sanchez's government is under pressure from the EU and a frustrated populace to fix the Ceuta crisis before elections on Nov 29.
Spanish authorities are housing 8,000 migrants in reception centres and processing asylum applications lodged by the majority of people remaining in Ceuta.

Several NGOs including Amnesty International have complained to the Spanish ombudsman that some of the more than 13,000 people the government says have returned to Morocco voluntarily since the middle of August were forced to leave, including non-Moroccans.

c64f7665838e2565: One in ten employees at SUSE are facing the chop due to "automation and AI," according to a memo dispatched by management at the privately owned open source software biz.
In an email to the 1,900 strong workforce on Monday - seen by The Register - CEO Dirk-Peter van Leeuwen, the former Red Hat exec who joined SUSE in March 2023, confirmed the "difficult news."

"We are announcing a reduction of SUSE’s global workforce of approximately 10 percent," he said. "These decisions are painful for our people, our culture, and our open source community, but they are necessary for us to adapt and build a sustainable, resilient SUSE for the long term."

Van Leeuwen says the business, bought by Swedish private equity provider EQT, decided to cut jobs after scrutinizing its "future strategy, required capabilities, and team structures." The rest of the organization will get a look at the fiscal year 2027 strategy on November 16.
He said in the message to staff:

"What is clear is that automation and AI are fundamentally shifting how software companies operate. AI capabilities are advancing exponentially, forcing us to radically reimagine our work. We have seen this trend already both inside our sector and in the wider economy. This means that the organizational design and cost base that SUSE is built on today will not carry us forward successfully.

"We are adapting. Across SUSE, modern tooling is already changing our daily workflows, enabling teams to move faster with less operational overhead and flatter reporting lines. The requirement for some existing roles has greatly diminished. Other roles will evolve over the next few years. This means we are accelerating investments in high priority areas, and deprioritizing others. These are hard, painful decisions to make, but necessary for our future."
As The Reg reported in 2025, SUSE doubled down on AI.

The specific roles at risk of redundancy were not outlined but SUSE claims it has considered where the people in those positions are "able to evolve, what they can stop doing, what they need to do more of - and decisions have been made on that basis."
Staff caught up in the redundancies will be informed by November 4, employee representatives nominated the following day, and one to one meetings will begin at the start of next week.

Van Leeuwen says in the internal memo that the job cuts are a "reflection of shifting organizational needs, not your talent or commitment. You have tackled hard infrastructure and open source challenges that power critical enterprise systems around the world.
"Any organization will be fortunate to have your expertise."

Back in September, we reported that the company was asking old hands if they would take "voluntary separation." It seems not enough people chose to walk through the door, so instead, they're getting thrown through it instead. SUSE "geckos" in the Czech Republic may be glad they joined a trade union.

Back in 2018, EQT bought SUSE from Microfocus for $2.5 billion. EQT floated SUSE on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange in 2021 with slightly disappointing results. A couple of years later, new CEO Dirk-Peter van Leeuwen took over, and later in 2023, EQT chose to take the company private again.
The commercial context is that in March SUSE's corporate owner EQT was reportedly considering selling it off again. ®
d7983a17de2f9afc: BEIJING: China stepped up diplomatic efforts on Monday to resolve the Middle East crisis, urging a return to the negotiating table in back-to-back meetings with Iranian, Omani and Saudi officials in Beijing.

The meetings come days after US president Donald Trump issued a fresh war threat more than eight months into the conflict, which was triggered by US-Israeli strikes on Iran and has at times spilled over into neighbouring countries.

Beijing supports Tehran in "safeguarding its own sovereignty and security", foreign minister Wang Yi told Ali Bagheri Kani, the deputy secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, according to a Chinese statement.

Wang later called for dialogue to end the conflict "while safeguarding regional energy security and the safety of shipping lanes", as he met with Saudi National security adviser Musaad bin Mohammad al-Aiban.
China, a top economic partner of Iran, has long sought a detente in the months-long conflict that has disrupted global shipping.
Trump said on Saturday that the US had knocked out much of Iran's military but still has to "take care of" one or two targets, with Tehran warning of reprisals if attacked.
"All parties should... in a spirit of reason and pragmatism, focus on a political solution rather than once again resorting to armed conflict," Wang told Bagheri Kani, according to the statement.
China's foreign ministry had not previously announced the visit by Bagheri Kani to Beijing.
President Xi Jinping also met Oman's sultan for talks in Beijing on Monday - the first visit to China by the Gulf nation's head of state since diplomatic ties were established.
Xi told Haitham bin Tariq that China was ready to "contribute to peace, stability and prosperity in the region".
The Chinese leader said that the Middle East should not become a "wrestling ground for major-country rivalry and geopolitical conflicts", state news agency Xinhua reported.

Later this month, Beijing will send its Middle East envoy to Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia as a part of "shuttle diplomacy visits... aimed at promoting peace talks (and) easing tensions", a Chinese foreign ministry spokesman told a news briefing.

Loke said the federal government had also fulfilled demands under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) by returning port authority powers to the state.
On land transport, he said the ministry had provided direct funding for public transport in Sarawak, which had not previously received such funding.
The BAS.MY (http://bas.my/) service was introduced in Kuching, with hopes of expanding it to other areas in the future, he said.

1cf79381fce79c7e: KUALA LUMPUR: Rural road development projects worth RM1.7 billion in Sabah have not been cancelled but postponed pending a review and realignment of allocation ceilings, said Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Sabah and Sarawak Affairs) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud.

"I stand by my statement that these projects have not been cancelled; they have only been postponed, and this has been explained in detail by the Finance Minister II.

"When the matter was raised in this House, people outside started asking questions, and the media asked as well. So, I had to respond based on the available facts. Alhamdulillah, the Finance Minister II has provided a clear explanation for our mutual understanding," he said when winding up the committee-stage debate on the Supply Bill 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat.

The status of the projects had previously sparked controversy and questions following allegations of conflicting statements regarding the postponement of 13 rural road infrastructure projects, particularly in Sabah and Sarawak.

Earlier, Datuk Seri Wilfred Madius Tangau (Upko-Tuaran), when interjecting, sought clarification on the actual status of the 13 projects following a statement allegedly made by the deputy prime minister that the projects had been cancelled.
He also questioned the role of the Sabah and Sarawak Affairs portfolio in championing the issue, given that the explanation had come from the Finance Ministry.

Datuk Willie Mongin (GPS-Puncak Borneo), who also interjected, claimed that contractors in his constituency had informed him of receiving letters cancelling rural road development projects, and called for the matter to be addressed transparently and consistently.

He said the proposal took into account the issue of 245 medical officers who had received placement letters but failed to report for duty in the state.

"We must ensure that students admitted to UMS medical programmes are Sabahans. If Sabah-born students are qualified, especially those with good academic results, this will help ensure that they remain in the state and serve in Sabah," he said.

66d773cc7406ff89: SHAH ALAM: The Selangor Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) disposed of 37.3 tonnes of illicit drugs of various types valued at RM1.71 billion today.
Federal NCID director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the exhibits were linked to 6,526 investigation papers involving cases from 2009 to 2025, all of which were fully resolved.

He said the drugs being disposed of included 33.5 tonnes of syabu (methamphetamine), 714 kg of ketamine, 104 kg of cannabis, 14 kg of ecstasy pills, nine kg of heroin, five kg of Erimin 5, one kg of Yaba pills, and 458 litres of MDMA.

"The disposal process will be carried out at a clinical waste treatment plant in Kuala Langat, where all exhibits will be completely destroyed in a controlled manner through high-tech and safe incineration," he said during a press conference at the Selangor police contingent headquarters.
Also in attendance was Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar.
Meanwhile, Hussein said 45.7 tonnes of solid drugs and 60,880 litres of liquid drugs worth approximately RM1.93 billion were disposed nationwide.
"Of that total, Selangor recorded the highest disposal value at RM1.71 billion, followed by Sabah with RM120.4 million and Johor with RM40.02 million," he said.
Hussein said the NCID also disposed of 13,342 narcotics investigation papers nationwide involving cases from 1991 to 2025.
"Of that figure, 90 per cent were cases were prosecuted and sentenced in court, eight per cent were acquitted, and two per cent involved seizures without arrest.
"Selangor recorded the highest number of disposed investigation papers at 6,526 cases, followed by Sarawak with 2,383 cases, and Perak with 2,069 cases," he said.
On enforcement, Hussein said from January to October this year, the NCID recorded 184,732 cases involving 205,536 arrests nationwide in its crackdown on drug trafficking and abuse.

"During the same period, the NCID seized over 39.1 tonnes of solid drugs and 31,176.56 litres of liquid drugs, while substances seized under the Poisons Act 1952 amounted to 47 tonnes and 112,600.94 litres.
"The total value of the seized drugs and poisons is RM2.96 billion," he said.

39bfde30fcb9d407: BRUSSELS: Dozens of Belgian grocery stores and an Ikea superstore saw their refrigerator temperatures soar on Monday, with several of the firms involved confirming they had been hit by a cyberattack.
It is the latest in a series of cyberattacks on store refrigerators and suspicious actions around the supermarkets across Europe.
A handful of Swedish supermarkets saw temperatures in their refrigerators and freezers soar early Monday, Swedish chains Ica and Coop said without giving a cause.
Major French retailers said on Oct 12 that hundreds of store refrigeration systems were hit by a cyberattack, which forced them to throw out spoiled food and raised food security fears.
Carrefour Belgium reported disruption in about 15 of its 700 stores in Belgium. "It's a cyberattack, there is no other reason," said Mich Vergauwen, a spokesman for Carrefour Belgium.
An Ikea Belgium spokeswoman likewise said a cyberattack hit its store in Mons, southwestern Belgium, causing the temperature of freezers to rise suddenly in the early hours of Monday.
It is the only Ikea store affected because it uses a different service provider than others in Belgium, the spokeswoman added, without identifying the provider.
The Delhaize supermarket chain meanwhile said refrigeration systems in "dozens" of its stores were affected by an IT incident.
Delhaize did not specify the cause, but an AFP correspondent visiting one shop at Bortmeerbeek, northeast of Brussels, saw refrigerators and freezers empty with a sign blaming hackers.
"Due to cyberattacks, there will be no products on the refrigerated or freezer shelves. We offer our sincere apologies," Delhaize said.

The Colruyt and Intermarche supermarket chains likewise told AFP they had been hit by technical problems affecting fridges in five and around 15 stores respectively, without confirming if a cyberattack was suspected.
"In some cases, it involved only a single refrigerator, so the impact was quite limited," an Intermarche spokesman said, adding that the incidents took place overnight Sunday-to-Monday.
The issue is not limited to Belgium.
The Swedish chains ICA and Coop said they were looking into the cause of their temperature soars that forced them to throw away food.
One ICA store at Sjobo in southern Sweden posted on Facebook, however, that its fridges and freezers had "been hacked and they set the temperature at 50 degrees" Celsius.
More than 500 supermarkets were targeted in the French attack on Oct 12. The equipment was provided by Danish company, Danfoss.

196acab46e8fed38: KUALA NERUS: The Education Ministry is stepping up preparations for the northeast monsoon to ensure Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) candidates in flood-prone areas can sit their examinations safely.

Education (School Operations Sector) deputy director-general Datuk Zainal Abas said the annual operation, named Ops Payung, was aimed at ensuring candidates in flood-affected areas could take their examinations without disruption.
He said candidates in areas at risk of flooding would be given special arrangements during the written examinations.

"For example, SPM candidates living on islands in Terengganu will be brought to the mainland and accommodated in boarding schools. This will prevent them from having to cross rough seas during the monsoon season to reach their examination centres.

"It will also provide a safer and more suitable working environment for teachers serving as examination personnel," he told reporters after the Terafecta Digital Luminaries Awards ceremony organised by the Terengganu Education Department at Dewan Jubli Perak, Bandar Baru Kuala Nerus.

Zainal said the ministry was also coordinating preparations with the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), state and district disaster management committees and other relevant agencies to assist areas at risk of flooding.
On schools designated as temporary relief centres, he said Nadma allocated more than RM7 million this year to help the ministry improve their facilities.
The allocation covered toilet repairs and school maintenance to ensure the facilities were in good condition to accommodate flood victims.
"Recently, we were also informed that Nadma would provide an additional RM5 million to support the ministry's post-northeast monsoon efforts," he said.
He advised schools, parents and students to remain vigilant and take the necessary safety precautions throughout the monsoon season.
Parents, particularly those living in flood-prone areas, were urged to keep a close watch on their children to prevent accidents.

"Children playing in floodwaters or near drains during floods can put themselves in danger. Parents should therefore pay closer attention to their children's safety. Health and hygiene must also be prioritised," he said.
Zainal said the ministry was also ready to deploy its Smart Support Team (SST), comprising counselling teachers, to provide mental health support programmes and activities for primary school pupils.
The Academic Support Team (AST) would also assist students affected by floods, including by providing academic support at temporary relief centres.

"Although the school holidays begin on Dec 5, these teams can still be deployed to flood relief centres if schools are affected by floods in November, particularly to support examination candidates," he said.

He expressed hope that preparations and coordination with Nadma, state disaster management committees, the police, the Civil Defence Force and other agencies would proceed smoothly to address any eventuality during the monsoon season.
The 2026 SPM written examinations will be held from Nov 23 to Dec 17, while the northeast monsoon began on Oct 27 and is expected to continue until March 2027.

14b029b9df339adc: BRUSSELS: Michael Carrick brushed off suggestions he has just two games left as Manchester United boss as he prepares his underperforming side for Tuesday's Champions League clash against Roma.

Carrick's position at Old Trafford is increasingly precarious following Saturday's 2-0 defeat at Chelsea, which extended United's winless run in all competitions to nine games -- their longest such run in 42 years.
The club are just one place above the Premier League relegation zone after taking a mere seven points from their nine matches so far this season.
They are 20th in the Champions League table following a dismal 4-1 defeat away at Como last month. Only the top 24 teams will progress beyond the league phase.

Former United and England midfielder Carrick was asked at his pre-match press conference on Monday whether he felt he had just two games left at the helm - the match against Roma and Sunday's clash with Aston Villa.
There is an international break after the Villa game.
"No, not at all," said the 45-year-old, in his first full season in charge of United. "If you look into the future, you never know what's going to happen.
"I don't know what's going to happen. That doesn't change the way I feel, how we're preparing for the game tomorrow.
"I'm actually really looking forward to the game, can't wait for the game tomorrow. You might think I'm crazy with the results we've had and what's going on, but I genuinely can't wait," he said.
Carrick said the dressing room was in "a good place" despite the terrible start to the season.
"Perception is a funny thing. You can make things look all sorts of different ways and think about all sorts of different things," he said.

"I've said it before, the commitment of the players to the club, to me, to each other, I don't question that at all. We need to play better, we can make better decisions, but commitment is not a thing at all," he added.
He defended United's Argentine centre-back Lisandro Martinez, who was sent off in United's defeat at Stamford Bridge.
"Things happen in football, sometimes you do things, sometimes you make decisions, sometimes you make mistakes, sometimes it goes well for you, but the commitment is not an issue for sure."
Carrick has happy personal memories of facing Roma as a member of Alex Ferguson's team, scoring twice in United's 7-1 quarter-final second-leg triumph in the Champions League in 2007.
"It was a magical night, I have to say," he recalled. "It was one of the best nights, one of the best games, one of the best atmospheres I've been fortunate enough to witness.
"The fact that I scored a couple and that was very unusual gives me great memories, but it was more the emotion of the night, I have to say, it was a special one," he said.

65e9b7c03bef310f: Cyberattacks on both Russia’s and Ukraine’s emergency alert apps resulted in fake messages about missile and nuclear strikes broadcast to the public.
Officials from both countries confirmed the attacks, which occurred at similar times, on Sunday evening.
According to public statements and messages sent via social media, Ukraine’s alert app was hit first, with the country’s Air Force quick to dispel nuclear fears.
"The Air Alert app has likely been compromised," it said via Telegram at around 2100 UTC. "There is no radiation threat! Stay calm, follow our messages on our channel!"
At around 0030 UTC on Monday, Russia's Ministry of Emergency Situations confirmed the country’s app had also been abused, with fake messages sent to citizens' devices.

"Attention! The Russian Ministry of Emergency Situations' mobile app has been subjected to a massive cyberattack, allowing attackers to send fake information to the public," it said, also via Telegram. "Work is currently underway to patch the vulnerability and restore normal operation."

The ministry issued an update around 90 minutes later, saying the app was once again functioning normally, and pointing out that an attack on the app was not the same as a compromise of the state’s national alert system.

"Citizens are alerted through primary channels: regional and municipal alert systems (sirens, loudspeakers), communication networks (SMS messaging), and television and radio broadcasts. The mobile app is merely an additional, supporting information service," it stated.

Ukraine's Ministry of Digital Affairs also issued a public announcement reminding citizens about how to receive emergency warnings while its “Alarm!” app was down. These include enabling iOS and Android emergency alerts, state-controlled sirens, and other official sources, such as the official social media accounts of Ukraine's government.

According to the messages sent to devices after the compromise of Ukraine's alert app, the fake warnings pertained to various threats, such as street fights in Kyiv, chemical attacks, and radiation hazards.

Alerts about the threat of nuclear fallout from official government warning systems would normally lead to panic, however, one of the earliest messages sent to citizens was written in Russian and referenced the "Oreshnik" missile, which was an immediate signal that the message may not be genuine.
Equivalent alerts sent to Russian citizens also warned of impending nuclear strikes "at all regions of Russia," referencing "P1-Sun," the name of a Ukrainian attack drone.

Oleksander Merezhko, who chairs the Ukrainian parliament's foreign affairs committee and noted the suspicious Russian-language alert, told the BBC the attack was almost certainly part of Russia's cyber war.
"It's a very unpleasant fact but it is part of cyber war and people in Ukraine understand that," he said. "It is possible and we are quite prepared for such possibilities."
Russia has not explicitly blamed Ukraine for the attack on its app, and official sources say the app is running as normal.
Ukraine's announcement of the alert app cyberattack came almost simultaneously with the official conclusion of a six-day ceasefire in Kherson.
Russia agreed to the rare temporary suspension of conflict to allow hundreds of Ukrainians to evacuate the Russian-occupied city of Olehsky.
Russia did not agree to a proposed extension of the ceasefire, which officially ended at around 2100 UTC – around the same time Ukrainians began receiving fake warning messages. ®

Gordon said his team deserved to win the Clasico, which Real Madrid claimed with a late goal from Kylian Mbappe as Barca's defence crumbled.

"For me were there much better team in the game, we had all the ball, all the possession, the better chances, but we were a slight bit off our best game. It cost us in the end, we conceded two very bad goals.

"Against this kind of opposition and this level of player, it can really hurt you in these games. We'll learn for next time, and I'm really excited to play these types of teams again to show what we can do," Gordon said.
Barca host Premier League side Aston Villa on Tuesday as they aim to get back on track in the Champions League, before visiting Atletico Madrid on Sunday in La Liga.
"I'm always motivated the same... the fact they're English doesn't make it more motivating for me," said Gordon ahead of Villa's visit to Camp Nou.
"They're a very good team... they have a great coach (Unai Emery), one of the best in the world... it's going to be a very difficult game," Gordon said.
Villa hold a 100% record so far in the Champions League, defeating Viking, Fenerbahce and Club Brugge.
Barcelona signed Gordon from Newcastle in the summer for a fee which could rise to €80 million (US$89m).
The 25-year-old has three goals and five assists in 13 appearances for Barcelona across all competitions, but said his best is yet to come.
"It's a big change, a new team, it's been a massive change for me and my family," added Gordon.

"I've started well, but like I've said numerous times, I can do more. It will take some time to grow, feel settled, and then when this happens I think you'll see the very best of me, which you definitely haven't seen so far," Gordon said.
50ad86a3848a9673: The transcript from this week’s, MiB: Rich Steinmeier LPL CEO on The Future of Financial Advice, is below.
